text: Does each additional contact call to the same customer in a campaign reduce the chance that the customer subscribes to a term deposit?

45,211 customer records from phone campaigns of a Portuguese bank. A plain analysis says more calls to the same person means fewer subscriptions, so cap them. But who gets called many times is not random: hard-to-reach customers, the month, the contact channel and earlier campaigns all differ. Observational data, no planted effect; a live run only.

Does the new checkout increase the conversion rate?

Fourteen days of checkout sessions, randomised by user. The default analysis shows a significant lift and says ship. But employees and QA testers placed test orders through the new checkout, and one defensible filter removes them and erases the lift.

Does the relation between religiosity and well-being depend on perceived cultural norms of religion?

105 research teams analysed this dataset; 68 found that the religiosity-well-being relation grows with perceived cultural norms with an interval above zero. The default analysis gives interaction beta = 0.045 (95% CI 0.026 to 0.063), p < 0.001, n = 10,535. The verdict changes in 1 of 15 universes; the nearest is Pooled OLS, robust errors: interaction beta = 0.018 (95% CI -0.000 to 0.037), p = 0.056, n = 10,535.

Do religious people self-report greater well-being?

110 research teams analysed this dataset; 110 found that religiosity goes with higher well-being with an interval above zero. The default analysis gives beta = 0.140 (95% CI 0.119 to 0.160), p < 0.001, n = 10,535. Borges found no defensible flip in 40 universes.

Are soccer referees more likely to give red cards to dark-skin-toned players than to light-skin-toned players?

Twenty-nine teams analysed this dataset and disagreed on whether referees card dark-skinned players more. The default analysis gives OR 1.34 (95% CI 1.13 to 1.58): bias detected. No single analytic choice reverses that and no pair does; it takes three together, such as a full covariate set, frequent referees only and player-clustered errors, to land on no clear evidence (OR 1.20 to 1.25). The one single flip that existed, restricting to low-bias referees, is not defensible.
